reply_text:
Gist: "Correction" was my loose shorthand, and it's worse than loose. The family is really "your turns where 象 cited `apparatus/done-is-observed-running`". That pattern says something counts as done only when the live system is seen doing it, not when the commit lands. So these are turns where you report that something claimed as done isn't showing up live. A better name would be "live-gap reports", and I'll use that from now on. Membership comes only from 象's citation, though, and not every member fits.

**Four of the thirteen turns:**

| Turn | Your words | Fits? |
|---|---|---|
| turn-g9JGYE, to me | "frame 89 / 89 is still pretty much empty, not sure what happened there" | Yes |
| turn-D2GnQn, to claude-19 | "…about.html is still showing the other order so we need to deploy the reorder on futon7a" | Yes |
| turn-MCErMC, to claude-1 | "…we validated a lean model and ran many tests and still find the system abstains from running" | Yes |
| turn-iNKHir, to me | "if it is really a stepper with Elephant-2000 semantics we should be able to demonstrate things like rewinding…" | No: that's a request with a critique, not a report that something done isn't live. 象 cited the pattern anyway. |

**What the rule would say:** after an agent's turn that claimed work (it committed), you report a gap between that claim and the live system. The agent then produces follow-up work, which in the records is another commit. The War Machine can use a rule like that, because its condition is about the work and the records, not about you speaking.

**What this means for the numbers:** membership is noisy. With 7 complete records, one misfiled turn like iNKHir changes the result noticeably. So the running packet should also check membership, not just recover missing turns. I'll do that check myself when codex-5 reports: read each of the 13 turns against the pattern's condition (claimed done, not seen working) and drop the ones that don't fit before any rerun. I'll also rename the family in the notes.

Both causes check out (same text, session and second, with no origin field). Now the membership check I promised: reading all 13 turns against the pattern's condition.Gist: The missing records are mostly recoverable. 12 of the 15 turns can be joined, which puts the live-gap family (formerly "corrections") at 12 of 12 and go-aheads at 32 of 35. That's past the 10 records needed for a real test. codex-5 is now applying the fix and rebuilding the corpus. The stricter test is written down before any measurement.

**What codex-5 found** (bbdaf0e8, which codex-5's own commit signed as `Agent-Id: codex-5`):
- **10 turns:** your older turns are stored without an "origin" field, so they were filtered out as not-yours.
- **1 turn:** the turn record was written 91 seconds before the evidence row, outside the 60-second matching window.
- **1 turn:** it only looked like a session's first turn, because the older turns before it had been filtered out.
- **3 turns:** genuinely absent from the evidence store, so not recoverable.

I checked two of these myself with direct reads. Same text, same session, same second, and no origin field.

**Membership, read by hand:** I read all 13 cited fragments against the pattern's condition, that something claimed as done isn't seen working. 12 fit. The one that doesn't is turn-2GmY4p, which approves a diagram. That also corrects what I told you last turn: turn-iNKHir *does* fit, because the fragment 象 cited is your "various attempts at having the inbox-zero service actually work… not convinced".

**Written before measuring** (d5eabe88):
- the rename to "live-gap";
- the exclusion of turn-2GmY4p;
- the stricter test:
  - the baseline is matched on the same condition;
  - the predicted fact is chosen inside each held-out fold;
  - p < 0.05/3;
  - the verdict carries its p-value, which is claude-1's loading requirement.

**Now running** (job `invoke-1790742658857-28259-4a8de951`, park `park-3727f7e9-d91e-49d7-981a-f049a05adbed`): the matching fix and a rebuilt corpus.
- **Guard:** an old turn is admitted only when its full text matches exactly one of your records in the same session. Planted tests cover a duplicate text and a text from another session.
- **The stepper:** its own frames mustn't change as a side effect.

Once I've reviewed it, the induction runs under the new test.

Gist: The corpus is rebuilt and I've accepted it. The live-gap family now has complete records for all 12 of its turns, up from 7, and go-aheads have 32 of 35. codex-5 is now running the induction under the stricter test I wrote down before this measurement. So we'll get a p-value, not just "better than a weak baseline".

**What I checked** (104bfe1f):
- **Files:** the corpus script, its tests and the new corpus, plus an optional parameter in `turn_frames.py`. The parameter is off by default, so the stepper's frames don't change.
- **Tests:** 23 pass. Both uniqueness guards fail their test when I plant non-unique matching, one guard at a time.
- **Membership:** the live-gap family is exactly 12 turns, with turn-2GmY4p excluded.
- **The old corpus:** kept alongside, for comparison.

**Running now** (job `invoke-1790742838724-28273-4df83520`, park `park-c3c68426-0d19-4598-b176-667796bb044b`):
- **The test:** the baseline is matched on the same condition, and the predicted fact is chosen inside each held-out fold. A result must reach p < 0.0167, which is 0.05 split across the three candidate facts.
- **Planted tests:** one for each of those rules.

When it's back, I'll recompute one p-value by hand. If the live-gap rule passes, it's the first candidate for the War Machine to load in a plan-only run (criterion 6), and I'll send it to claude-1. If it doesn't pass, you'll get the numbers anyway.

Gist: Under the stricter test, neither rule passes. Go-aheads: 20 of 22 were followed by a commit, against 240 of 343 for comparable turns, p = 0.021. That misses the corrected threshold of 0.0167 narrowly. Live-gap reports show no effect at all: 6 of 9 against 177 of 253. The reason is that "a commit followed" is the wrong outcome to measure for this pattern. Its whole point is that a commit isn't proof something works; being seen working live is. Shall I have codex-5 find out which records show something being activated (a reload, restart or deploy, or you later confirming it works), as the outcome to measure instead?

**What I checked** (ca6e0c09):
- **Declaration:** the stricter test's written declaration is unchanged; the note has only additions after it.
- **p-values:** I recomputed both myself with an exact binomial, 0.02053 and 0.72875, which match.
- **Planted bugs:** each makes its test fail:
  - a threshold of 0.05 instead of 0.05/3;
  - a baseline not matched on the same condition.
- **The earlier results:** the old test mode still reproduces them byte for byte.
- **Live-gap sample size:** only 9 of the 12 turns met the rule's condition. That's also below the declared 10, so it's formally "too few to judge" as well as showing no effect.

**What this says:** measured honestly, 象's labels don't yet predict what happens next any better than the base rate, at least with commits and parks as the outcome. For live-gap, that's the expected result for the wrong outcome, not evidence against the pattern. The go-ahead result is close enough to be worth rerunning with more turns.

**The War Machine:** nothing goes to claude-1 for loading, since no rule passed. The reading is in the C2 note (5f7315d1).
